We have examined Vercel Inc.’s (“Vercel” or the “service organization”) accompanying description of its Vercel AI
Cloud system, in Section 3, throughout the period July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025, (the “description”), based on the
criteria for a description of a service organization’s system in DC section 200, 2018 Description Criteria for a
Description of a Service Organization’s System in a SOC 2® Report (AICPA, Description Criteria) (“description
criteria”), and the suitability of the design and operating effectiveness of controls stated in the description throughout
the period July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025, to provide reasonable assurance that Vercel’s service commitments and
system requirements were achieved based on the trust services criteria relevant to security, availability, and
confidentiality (“applicable trust services criteria”) set forth in TSP section 100, Trust Services Criteria for Security,
Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (AICPA, Trust Services Criteria).

o,

20

25

-10

-15

Vercel uses various subservice organizations for cloud hosting services. The description indicates that
complementary subservice organization controls that are suitably designed and operating effectively are necessary,
along with controls at Vercel, to achieve Vercel’s service commitments and system requirements based on the
applicable trust services criteria. The description presents Vercel’s controls, the applicable trust services criteria,
and the types of complementary subservice organization controls assumed in the design of Vercel’s controls. The
description does not disclose the actual controls at the subservice organizations. Our examination did not include
the services provided by the subservice organizations, and we have not evaluated the suitability of the design or
operating effectiveness of such complementary subservice organization controls.

Vercel is responsible for its service commitments and system requirements and for designing, implementing, and

and system requirements were achieved. Vercel has provided the accompanying assertion, in Section 2,

threaten the achievement of the service organization’s service commitments and system requirements.
Service Auditor’s Responsibilities
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the description and on the suitability of design and operating
effectiveness of controls stated in the description based on our examination. Our examination was conducted in
accordance with attestation standards established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
(AICPA). Those standards require that we plan and perform our examination to obtain reasonable assurance about
whether, in all material respects, the description is presented in accordance with the description criteria and the
controls stated therein were suitably designed and operated effectively to provide reasonable assurance that the
service organization’s service commitments and system requirements were achieved based on the applicable trust
services criteria. We believe that the evidence we obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a reasonable
basis for our opinion.

2

An examination of the description of a service organization’s system and the suitability of the design and operating
effectiveness of controls involves the following:
Obtaining an understanding of the system and the service organization’s service commitments and system
requirements.

•

Assessing the risks that the description is not presented in accordance with the description criteria and that
controls were not suitably designed or did not operate effectively.

•

Performing procedures to obtain evidence about whether the description is presented in accordance with
the description criteria.

•

Performing procedures to obtain evidence about whether controls stated in the description were suitably
designed to provide reasonable assurance that the service organization achieved its service commitments
and system requirements based on the applicable trust services criteria.

•

Testing the operating effectiveness of controls stated in the description to provide reasonable assurance
that the service organization achieved its service commitments and system requirements based on the
applicable trust services criteria.

•

Evaluating the overall presentation of the description.

SECTION 3

DESCRIPTION OF THE
SYSTEM

7

OVERVIEW OF OPERATIONS
Company Background
Vercel Inc. (Vercel) is the AI Cloud, offering a fullstack cloud platform for building, deploying, and running web
experiences, intelligent applications, and the agents behind them. The company provides hosting services,
serverless technology, developer workflows, and v0, a leading AI web development assistant. Founded in 2015 by
Guillermo Rauch, Vercel maintains Next.js, AI SDK, and shadcn/ui.

6:4
6.7
09
Z

Description of Services Provided

-15

T2
2:0

The Vercel AI Cloud platform provides a range of AI-native tools and services for developers, including hosting,
serverless functions, deployment automation, primitives, and v0, an AI web development assistant. Additionally,
Vercel provides managed infrastructure features, such as automatic scaling, custom domains, analytics, and
Content Delivery Network (CDN) support, allowing developers to build frontend, backend, and AI applications that
can handle large amounts of traffic.

25

-10

PRINCIPAL SERVICE COMMITMENTS AND SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

20

Principal Service Commitments

pla

ne
ra.
i

o,

Vercel designs its processes and procedures related to the AI Cloud to meet its objectives for its services. Those
objectives are based on the service commitments that Vercel makes to user entities, the laws and regulations that
govern the provision of Vercel services, and the financial, operational, and compliance requirements that Vercel
has established for the services. The services of Vercel are subject to the relevant regulatory and industry
information and data security requirements in which Vercel operates.

,m

ike
g@

Security, availability, and confidentiality commitments to user entities are documented and communicated in
Vercel’s Terms of Service (ToS), Data Processing Agreement (DPA), the service level commitments, and other
publicly available security and support documentation. The principal security, availability, and confidentiality
commitments are standardized and include the following:
Vercel operates on a shared responsibility model with customers for providing services related to customer
data, encryption and data integrity, authentication, and log management. Vercel is responsible for the
security and availability of the underlying infrastructure used to provide its services, including compute,
storage, and networking environments.

•

Vercel will implement and maintain technical and organizational security measures designed to protect
customer data from security incidents and to preserve the security and confidentiality of the customer data.

•

Vercel maintains customer data in an encrypted format at rest using advanced encryption standard (AES256) and in transit (transport layer security (TLS) 1.2 or higher).

•

Vercel monitors access to systems, applications, tools, and resources that process or store customer data,
including cloud services. Monitoring of security logs is centralized by the security team. Log activities are
investigated when necessary and escalated appropriately. User activity metrics are available to customers
within the services.

•

Vercel adheres to a change management process to administer changes to the production environment for
the services, including changes to its underlying software, applications, and systems. Monitors are in place
to notify the security team and other relevant stakeholders of changes made to critical infrastructure and
services that do not adhere to the change management processes.

•

Termination or expiration of the agreement serves as instruction for Vercel to delete customer data within
a commercially reasonable timeframe.

M

ike

Gu
ze
w

icz

•

8

•

Vercel agrees not to use confidential information for any purpose other than the purposes related to the
customer agreement.

•

Daily backups of customer data are performed, backups are retained redundantly across multiple
availability zones and encrypted in transit and at rest.

System Requirements

6:4
6.7
09
Z

Such requirements are communicated in Vercel’s policies and procedures, system design documentation, and
contracts with customers. Information security policies define an organization-wide approach to how systems and
data are protected. These include policies around how the service is designed and developed, how the system is
operated, how internal business systems and networks are managed, and how employees are hired, trained, and
managed. In addition to these policies, standard operating procedures have been documented on how to carry out
specific manual and automated processes required in the operation and development of the Vercel system.

People

Executive Management – responsible for overseeing company-wide activities, establishing, and
accomplishing goals, and overseeing objectives.

•

People Operations – responsible for Human Resources (HR) policies, practices, and processes with a focus
on key HR department delivery areas (e.g., talent acquisitions, employee retention, compensation,
employee benefits, performance management, employee relations and training, and development).

•

Product and Engineering – responsible for developing, implementing, and operating a healthy engineering
culture, maintaining availability of the product platform, and aligning to technical and security guidance in
providing a resilient product offering.

•

Information Technology (IT) – responsible for enabling employee access to official Vercel systems,
supporting employee employment lifecycle in partnership with People Operations.

•

Legal – responsible for procurement lifecycle with regards to customers and services utilized, reviewing
legal collateral, noting any deviations from standard legal documentation and on-standard contracts.

•

Security – responsible for developing, implementing, and operating appropriate technical security controls,
supporting overall information security and risk management lifecycle.

Procedures

,m

Access, Authentication, and Authorization

Gu
ze
w

icz

Access to system information, including confidential data, is protected by authentication and authorization
mechanisms. A standard build template is in place to guide personnel in commissioning new production systems.
Additionally, the production environment is segmented from other non-critical environments to help ensure that
confidential data is isolated from unrelated networks.

M

ike

Users accessing production systems are required to authenticate with a unique user account and enforce minimum
password requirements. Vercel utilizes Okta for single sign-on (SSO) to authenticate users to the AWS production
environment with a unique user account and predefined minimum password requirements with multi-factor
authentication (MFA). The AWS production environment utilizes the identity access management (IAM) console to
manage the SSO groups to production system resources. Users are added to predefined security groups to help
ensure role-based access privileges are enforced and access to data is segregated. For Microsoft Azure, security
keys and MFA are utilized as a means of authentication methods to the Microsoft Azure production environment,
including the Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB. Pre-defined access groups are utilized within Microsoft Azure to restrict
access based on pre-defined privileges. Administrative access privileges to the in-scope systems are restricted to
user accounts accessible by authorized personnel.
Access Requests and Access Suspension
Management has established controls to help ensure that access to data is restricted and provisioned based on the
concept of least privilege. Formal documentation is required for access requests and access suspensions to help
ensure activities are completed for the addition, modification, and suspension of system and software access
privileges. When a new employee is hired and has accepted a position at Vercel, user access provisioning and
10

onboarding requirements are documented as part of a standardized process. New hire access request forms
include relevant information related to the new employee, such as full name, job title, start date, and employment
eligibility requirements. Access request forms require approval from system owners for processing. Certain access
approvals are implicit based upon the job role. With the initiation of a new hire access request form, IT personnel
will create a corresponding entry in the ticketing system, which includes detailed onboarding activities completed
(e.g., providing the employee a laptop and e-mail account creation). If an employee requires additional access
privileges, a request would be submitted with approval from the relevant manager before the additional access
rights are provisioned to other Vercel systems.

6:4
6.7
09
Z

Upon notification of an employee termination, IT personnel complete a checklist to help ensure that employees do
not retain system access subsequent to their termination date. IT helps ensure SSO deactivation will occur in
alignment with the last working day or time provided by People Operations. IT personnel promptly remove any
corporate and/or production environment access for the terminated employee. In addition, to help ensure access
privileges are appropriate, a user access review is performed on a quarterly basis, including privileged users, to
help ensure that access to the in-scope systems and data is restricted to authorized personnel.
Network Security

T2
2:0

Security groups serving as virtualized firewall systems are in place to filter unauthorized inbound network traffic
from the Internet and deny any type of network connection that is not explicitly authorized. The security group rules
are reviewed on an annual basis to help ensure that only necessary connections are configured within the rulesets.

-15

Change Management

ike
g@

pla

ne
ra.
i

o,

20

25

-10

Vercel has a process in place to help provide reasonable assurance that unauthorized changes are not made to
production application systems. Vercel follows a standard change management process across its applications
and systems. Documented change control policies and procedures are in place to guide personnel in performing
changes to customer production systems. If a change is necessary to a production system, the engineering team
will document a change request ticket. Infrastructure and application change requests are tracked within the
ticketing system. Change details include, but are not limited to, the description of the change, details regarding the
criticality of the change, the timeframe for the implementation of the change, code review, and final approval.
Changes to system infrastructure and system / application software are developed and tested in an environment
separate from production. The testing environment utilizes non-production data. Virtual private clouds (VPCs) are
utilized to logically segregate the staging and production environments. Vercel also conducts bi-weekly change
management meetings where discussions are held regarding active product features and developments that are
underway for the Vercel AI Cloud. Members of the bi-weekly change meeting include team members from Security,
Engineering, and other key technical and executive leaders within Vercel.

Gu
ze
w

icz

,m

Vercel utilizes GitHub version control software to control code versioning and security throughout the code
development process. Write access privileges to source code libraries and administrative access privileges within
GitHub are restricted to user accounts accessible by authorized engineering or development personnel. Branch
protection rules are configured to systematically enforce peer review before a change is merged into the production
repository. The branch protection configurations are monitored via Datadog and are configured to notify IT security
personnel via Slack in the event that any of the branch protection configurations are modified.

M

ike

Once the software development standards have been met, code changes are configured to require peer review and
undergo automated testing procedures prior to being merged into the master branch. Vercel restricts the ability to
implement changes into the production environment to those individuals who require the ability to implement
changes as part of their job function. Additionally, a file integrity monitoring (FIM) tool is utilized to monitor changes
to the production environment and is configured to notify authorized personnel when changes to the production
environment occur. Administrative access to the FIM tool is restricted to authorized personnel which include highlevel engineering and security team members.
System Monitoring
Information resources are continuously monitored by the response team to help ensure secure operation and
availability of the system. Vercel utilizes cloud-based log management and monitoring systems, including an IDS,
to monitor the health of production systems, including capacity, availability, and security events. Monitoring
encompasses the availability and health of the AWS and Microsoft Azure systems (monitored by non-AWS and
Microsoft Azure resources / tools). This monitoring provides personnel with the awareness if there are any
11

performance or security incidents, including unauthorized network and security group changes. Event notifications
are configured to notify personnel when service thresholds are breached. Additionally, the IT security team actively
monitors the cloud production monitoring applications to help ensure the systems are operating properly. In the
event that a monitored system exceeds a pre-defined threshold, which is defined by operations, an automated
notification will be sent to the Response team for investigation. Any security incidents identified are reviewed by
incident response personnel, and a ticket is created, if necessary, to document the resolution of the security incident.
The incident management process is utilized to document incidents and resolutions.
Penetration Testing and Vulnerability Assessments

6:4
6.7
09
Z

Vercel utilizes a third-party vendor to perform annual penetration testing of production systems. Additionally, Vercel
security personnel utilize a third-party utility to perform a vulnerability scan of the production application on a daily
basis to identify threats within the production environment as well as to verify compliance with corporate policies.
Security vulnerabilities that are identified are triaged by security personnel and monitored through resolution.
Incident Response

25

-10

-15

T2
2:0

Incident response and escalation policies and procedures are documented to efficiently and effectively manage
unexpected incidents impacting the business. Vercel utilizes various communication channels for communicating
and tracking any identified incidents, including telephone, e-mail, and instant messaging. When an issue is
reported, an authorized security or engineering team member will examine the issue and determine whether or not
the incident requires escalation, and if the issue is a security incident, actions are taken to resolve the issue and
restore normal operations to affected systems. Additionally, postmortem reports that include the incident and impact
analysis, resolutions, lessons learned, and action items are documented. SEV1 and SEV2 incidents must have a
post-mortem report, with anything beyond a SEV2 or informational shall be at the discretion of the Incident Captain
or CISO.

20

Data Replication, Backup, and Disaster Recovery

,m

ike
g@

pla

ne
ra.
i

o,

The infrastructure is deployed into two distinct availability regions (with respect to each of the AWS and Microsoft
Azure platforms) to help ensure redundancy. Vercel maintains defined backup and recovery procedures. AWS’
and Microsoft Azure’s storage capabilities are utilized for primary data storage as well as backup and redundancy.
An automated backup of the production data is performed on at least a daily basis, and the data is stored in the
relevant AWS and Microsoft Azure platforms’ storage with replication across the respective secondary availability
zones / regions. In addition, AWS backups are encrypted at rest and in transit across the availability zones / regions.
As part of the cloud hosting services, Microsoft encrypts backups at rest and in transit. Backups of Vercel’s
production data help ensure systems and data are available for restoration in the event of a system failure or
disruption. Additionally, security personnel review backup system logs on a continuous basis.

M

Data

ike

Gu
ze
w

icz

Vercel has established a disaster recovery (DR) and business continuity plan for the Vercel AI Cloud. The DR plan
is designed to develop, test, and document a well-structured and easily understood plan which will help Vercel
personnel recover and restore operations as quickly and effectively as possible from a disaster or emergency
interruption to information systems and business operations. In addition, on at least an annual basis, Vercel
personnel perform a disaster recovery test in the form of tabletops, simulations, reenactments, or general company
impact risk-oriented asynchronous discussions, if a disaster has not occurred.

Customer business data is captured in the Vercel AI Cloud, including names and e-mail addresses. Customer and
confidential data is classified as restricted data. As such, this is governed by the confidentiality agreements
executed between Vercel and customers or vendors. Vercel’s data classification and handling requirements are
defined in the information security and data handling policies. Confidential data requires the highest level of security
in accordance with relevant security policies, regulations, and contractual requirements.
Data within the Vercel AI Cloud is generated and uploaded by customers. The transmission of confidential data is
secured via an Internet connection encrypted with the TLS protocol. Each customer is responsible for administering
their users and data, which includes the accuracy and timeliness of the data entered into the system. Production
customer data, including backup data, is stored in an encrypted format at rest utilizing AES-256 encryption. For
AWS production systems, access to the encryption keys is restricted to the authorized AWS console administrators.
12

As part of the Microsoft Azure cloud hosting services, Microsoft encrypts Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB’s by default
and restricts access to the encryption keys.

The control environment at Vercel is the foundation for the other areas of internal control. It sets the tone of the
organization and influences the control consciousness of its personnel. The components of the control environment
factors include the integrity and ethical values; management’s commitment to competence; its organizational

The control environment at Vercel is the foundation for the other areas of internal control. It sets the tone of the

factors include the integrity and ethical values, management’s commitment to competence; its organizational
structure; the assignment of authority and responsibility; and the oversight and direction provided by executive

Integrity and Ethical Values

ike
g@

ne

The effectiveness of controls cannot rise above the integrity and ethical values of the people who create, administer,
and monitor them. Integrity and ethical values are essential elements of the control environment, affecting the
design, administration, and monitoring of other components. Integrity and ethical behavior are the product of
Vercel’s ethical and behavioral standards, how they are communicated, and how they are reinforced in practices.
In addition, Vercel communicates values and behavioral standards to personnel through policy statements, codes
of conduct, and by example. Specific control activities that Vercel has implemented in this area are described
below:
Management formally documents the organizational policy statements that communicate entity values and
behavioral standards to personnel.

•

Employees are required to sign an acknowledgement form upon hire indicating that they have been given
access to the employee handbook and standards of employee conduct and understand their responsibility
for adhering to the associated policies and procedures.

•

Background screenings are performed for employees as a component of the hiring process.

•

Employees are required to sign a confidentiality statement upon hire agreeing not to disclose proprietary or
confidential information, including client information, to unauthorized parties.

•

An employee sanction procedure is in place and documented within the code of conduct communicating
that an employee may be terminated for noncompliance with a policy and/or procedure.

Vercel management defines competence as the knowledge and skills necessary to accomplish tasks that define
employees’ roles and responsibilities. As such, commitment to competence includes management’s consideration
of the competence levels for particular jobs and how those levels translate into requisite skills and knowledge.

New hire checklists are completed to guide the hiring process to help ensure that newly hired employees
are compliant with the company’s employment standards and corporate policies and procedures.

Employees are required to complete security awareness training, upon hire and annually thereafter, to
understand their obligations and responsibilities to comply with the corporate and business unit security
policies.

•

Management monitors compliance with training requirements on a continuous basis.

RISK ASSESSMENT

20

Objective Setting

ike
g@

pla

ne
ra.
i

o,

Information security risk management is the coordinated management of business operations, technology, and
intelligence to effectively manage and protect an organization's business information assets and operations from
information security threats. Information security threats typically occur through malicious external threat sources
including organized crime, nation states, hacktivists, etc., as well as inadvertent or intentional insider actions, with
different motives and a variety of attack methods.
Risk Identification and Analysis

Gu
ze
w

icz

,m

Vercel has placed a risk assessment process in operation to identify and manage risks that could affect the
organization's ability to provide reliable services for its user entities. As part of internal audit activities, Vercel
conducts quarterly enterprise risk assessments. This process requires management to identify significant risks in
their areas of responsibility and to implement measures to address those risks. Key members of the executive
management and operational teams meet on a quarterly basis to identify and review risks to the system. These
risks are documented within their risk matrix and risk register.

M

ike

Risk analysis is an essential process to the entity’s success. It includes identification of key business processes
where potential exposures of some consequence exist, as well as significant changes to those processes. Once
the significance and likelihood of risk have been assessed, management considers how the risk should be
managed. This involves judgment based on assumptions about the risk and reasonable analysis of costs
associated with reducing the level of risk.
Necessary actions are taken to reduce the significance or likelihood of the risk occurring and to identify the control
activities necessary to mitigate the risk. Management has identified these control activities and documented them
in the trust services criteria and related control activities section below. Additionally, management reviews the
assessed risk levels on a quarterly basis and documents the risk assessment in the quarterly risk programs.

16

Risk Factors
Management considers risks that can arise from both external and internal factors including the following:
External Factors
Technological developments

•

Changing customer needs or expectations

•

Competition that could alter marketing or service activities

•

New legislation and regulation that could force changes in policies and strategies

•

Natural catastrophes that could lead to changes in operations or information systems

•

Economic changes that could have an impact on management decisions

6:4
6.7
09
Z

•

Internal Factors
Significant changes in policies, processes, or personnel

•

Types of fraud, including incentives, pressures, opportunities, and rationalizations to commit fraud

•

A disruption in information systems processing

•

The quality of personnel hired, and methods of training utilized

•

Changes in management responsibilities

Potential for Fraud

pla

ne
ra.
i

Management considers the potential for fraud when assessing the risks to the company’s objectives. The potential
for fraud can occur in both financial and non-financial reporting. Other types of fraud include the misappropriation
of assets and illegal acts such as violations of governmental laws.

,m

ike
g@

Management realizes that the potential for fraud can occur when employees are motivated by certain pressures or
incentivized to commit fraud. The absence of controls, or ineffective controls, provides an opportunity for fraud
when combined with an incentive to commit fraud. Therefore, management considers fraud factors in each risk
evaluated during the risk assessment process.

Gu
ze
w

icz

Risk Mitigation

M

ike

Risk mitigation strategies include prevention and elimination through the implementation of internal controls and
transference through commercial, general, and umbrella insurance policies. Management personnel are required
to identify significant risks relating to their areas of responsibility and implement measures to mitigate those risks.
The organization has documented policies and procedures to guide personnel throughout this process. The
quarterly risk assessment and mitigation process also addresses risks arising from potential business disruptions.

TRUST SERVICES CRITERIA AND RELATED CONTROL ACTIVITIES
Integration with Risk Assessment
Along with assessing risks, management has identified and put into effect actions needed to address those risks.
In order to address risks, control activities have been placed into operation to help ensure that the actions are
carried out properly and efficiently. Control activities serve as mechanisms for managing the achievement of the
security, availability, and confidentiality categories.
17

Selection and Development of Control Activities
The applicable trust services criteria and related control activities are included in Section 4 of this report to eliminate
the redundancy that would result from listing the items in this section and repeating them in Section 4. Although
the applicable trust services criteria and related control activities are included in Section 4, they are, nevertheless,
an integral part of Vercel’s description of the system.
The description of the service auditor’s tests of operating effectiveness and the results of those tests are also
presented in Section 4, the Testing Matrices, adjacent to the service organization’s description of controls. The
description of the tests of operating effectiveness and the results of those tests are the responsibility of the service
auditor and should be considered information provided by the service auditor.

Pertinent information must be identified, captured, and communicated in a form and timeframe that enables
personnel to carry out their responsibilities. Information systems produce reports containing operational, financial,
and compliance-related information, which make it possible to run and control the business. They deal not only
with internally-generated data, but also information about external events, activities, and conditions necessary to
inform business decision-making and external reporting. Effective communication also must occur in a broader
sense, flowing down, across, and up the organization. Personnel must receive a clear message from top
management that control responsibilities must be taken seriously. They must understand their own role in the
internal control system, as well as how individual activities relate to the work of others. They must have a means
of communicating significant information upstream. There also needs to be effective communication with external
parties, such as customers, suppliers, regulators, and shareholders.

Management communicates and reinforces understanding of employee duties and control responsibilities as

can also be made electronically, verbally, and through the actions of management. Vercel has implemented various
methods of communication to help provide assurance that employees understand their individual roles and
responsibilities and that significant events are communicated. These methods include orientation for new
employees, training for employees, and the use of Slack and e-mail to communicate time-sensitive information. If
incidents are detected, personnel follow a documented incident management process, and security related
incidents additionally follow the security incident response process as needed. Incidents are documented within
the ticketing system and tracked by management until resolved. Formal procedure changes are distributed to
management before they are incorporated into the policy and distributed to relevant parties.

MONITORING

M

ike

Monitoring is a process that assesses the quality of internal control performance over time. It involves assessing
the design and operation of controls and taking necessary corrective actions. This process is accomplished through
ongoing activities, separate evaluation, or a combination of the two. Monitoring activities also include using
information from communications from external parties such as user entity complaints and regulatory comments
that may indicate problems or highlight areas in need of improvement. Management has implemented a selfassessment and compliance program to help ensure the controls are consistently applied as designed.
Ongoing Monitoring
Monitoring can be done in two ways: through ongoing activities or separate evaluations. The greater the degree
and effectiveness of ongoing monitoring, the less the need is for separate evaluations. Management determines
the need for separate evaluations by consideration given to the following: the nature and degree of changes
occurring and their associated risks; the competence and experience of the people implementing the controls; and
the results of the ongoing monitoring. Management has implemented a combination of ongoing monitoring and
separate evaluations, as deemed necessary, to help ensure that the internal control system maintains its
19

effectiveness over time. Management personnel are involved in the day-to-day functioning of each department and
provide hands-on training, coaching, and correction. The management team holds meetings on a periodic basis
within functional departments to discuss changes to the organization, changes to the production environment, and
incidents or events identified by personnel or user entities. Vercel performs internal vulnerability assessment on a
daily basis and external penetration testing with a third-party vendor on an annual basis. Security vulnerabilities
that are detected are triaged by the security team and monitored through remediation.
Separate Evaluations

6:4
6.7
09
Z

Management has implemented a self-assessment program to evaluate the performance of specific control activities
and processes over time and confirm that the in-scope controls were consistently applied as designed, including
whether manual controls were applied by individuals who have the competence and authority. As a result of
management’s risk analysis process, each control activity within scope has been assigned a risk level associated
with the assessed level of risk it is intended to mitigate. Controls that serve to mitigate multiple risks are assigned
the highest level of assessed risk among the pertinent risks.

-15

T2
2:0

Management has determined that each risk assignment or category, will require structured inquiry, observation,
inspection, or sample testing, or a combination of the aforementioned, based on the assigned risk level and the
nature of the control, whether automated or manual, and the frequency of application (e.g., constant, daily, weekly,
quarterly, etc.). For manual controls, the self-assessment is performed by a secondary individual different from the
individual that primarily applies the control; additionally, subordinates do not evaluate the application of manual
controls performed by their supervisors or managers. Specific control activities that Vercel has implemented in this
area are described below:
A formal risk assessment is performed on a quarterly basis. Risks that are identified are rated using a risk
evaluation process that accounts for changes in risk from the prior year, and are formally documented,
along with mitigation strategies, for management review.

•

Risk owners perform a review of their assigned controls on a quarterly basis during the risk assessment
process.

SECTION 4

TESTING MATRICES

22

TESTS OF OPERATING EFFECTIVENESS AND RESULTS OF TESTS
Scope of Testing
This report on the controls relates to the Vercel AI Cloud system provided by Vercel. The scope of the testing was
restricted to the Vercel AI Cloud system and its boundaries as defined in Section 3. Schellman conducted the
examination testing over the period July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025.
Tests of Operating Effectiveness

6:4
6.7
09
Z

The tests applied to test the operating effectiveness of controls are listed alongside each of the respective control
activities within the Testing Matrices. Such tests were considered necessary to evaluate whether the controls were
sufficient to provide reasonable, but not absolute, assurance that the applicable trust services criteria were achieved
during the period. In selecting the tests of controls, Schellman considered various factors including, but not limited
to, the following:
the nature of the control and the frequency with which it operates;

•

the control risk mitigated by the control;

•

the effectiveness of entity-level controls, especially controls that monitor other controls;

•

the degree to which the control relies on the effectiveness of other controls; and

•

whether the control is manually performed or automated.

20

25

-10

-15

T2
2:0

•

ne
ra.
i

o,

The types of tests performed with respect to the operational effectiveness of the control activities detailed in this
section are briefly described below:
Description

Inquiry

Inquired of relevant personnel with the requisite knowledge and experience regarding
the performance and application of the related control activity. This included in-person
interviews, telephone calls, e-mails, web-based conferences, or a combination of the
preceding.

Observation

Observed the relevant processes or procedures during fieldwork. This included, but
was not limited to, witnessing the performance of controls or evidence of control
performance with relevant personnel, systems, or locations relevant to the
performance of control policies and procedures.

Inspection

Inspected the relevant audit records. This included, but was not limited to, documents,
system configurations and settings, or the existence of sampling attributes, such as
signatures, approvals, or logged events. In some cases, inspection testing involved
tracing events forward to consequent system documentation or processes (e.g.,
resolution, detailed documentation, alarms, etc.) or vouching backwards for
prerequisite events (e.g., approvals, authorizations, etc.).

M

ike

Gu
ze
w

icz

,m

ike
g@

pla

Test Approach

Sampling
Consistent with American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) authoritative literature, Schellman
utilizes professional judgment to consider the tolerable deviation rate, the expected deviation rate, the audit risk,
the characteristics of the population, and other factors, in order to determine the number of items to be selected in
a sample for a particular test. Schellman, in accordance with AICPA authoritative literature, selected samples in
such a way that the samples were expected to be representative of the population. This included judgmental
selection methods, where applicable, to ensure representative samples were obtained.

23

System-generated population listings were obtained whenever possible to ensure completeness prior to selecting
samples. In some instances, full populations were tested in cases including but not limited to, the uniqueness of
the event or low overall population size.
Reliability of Information Provided by the Service Organization
Observation and inspection procedures were performed related to certain system-generated reports, listings, and
queries to assess the accuracy and completeness (reliability) of the information used in the performance of our
testing of the controls.

6:4
6.7
09
Z

Test Results

20

25

-10

-15

T2
2:0

The results of each test applied are listed alongside each respective test applied within the Testing Matrices. Test
results not deemed as control deviations are noted by the phrase “No exceptions noted.” in the test result column
of the Testing Matrices. Any phrase other than the aforementioned, constitutes either a test result that is the result
of non-occurrence, a change in the application of the control activity, or a deficiency in the operating effectiveness
of the control activity. Testing deviations identified within the Testing Matrices are not necessarily weaknesses in
the total system of controls, as this determination can only be made after consideration of controls in place at user
entities and subservice organizations, if applicable, and other factors. Control considerations that should be
implemented by subservice organizations in order to complement the control activities and achieve the applicable
trust services criteria are presented in the “Subservice Organizations” section within Section 3.
